basis: Severe joint hypermobility, congenital hip dislocation and fragile hyperextensible skin define aEDS; motor delay does not establish primary neurologic damage.
Developmental impairment in all; VSD 6/10, skeletal malformations >=3/10 and hypodontia 3/10 support involvement; hearing impairment 2/10 excluded.
Inherited triglyceride storage disorder; skeletal myopathy occurs in >30% across the principal forms. Ichthyosis and hepatic damage vary substantially by subtype.
Central movement disorder causing myoclonus and dystonia; abnormal muscle movements do not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.
Non-syndromic congenital absence of all four limbs; syndromic visceral abnormalities are not established by this concept.
Glycosylation is a metabolic process; this heterogeneous umbrella does not establish common damage to any particular additional organ.
Lysosomal cystine storage with defining kidney and eye damage; myopathy 80-99% and rickets/osteomalacia 30-79%. Organ enlargement alone does not establish hepatic or splenic dysfunction.
Malignant vascular endothelial tumour; no specific skin or visceral site is established.
Vitamin K deficiency causes defective coagulation; impaired factor production does not establish intrinsic liver damage. Intracranial injury is not universal across forms.
TPP1 lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss develop in most patients over the typical course.
PFN1-associated motor neuron degeneration; muscle wasting, dysphagia and respiratory weakness result from denervation rather than direct muscle or lung disease.
Oral, limb and epiglottic malformations define OFD VIII; mild intellectual impairment is a defining feature despite unavailable frequency. Ocular involvement is insufficiently established.
Named vertebral, cardiac, renal and limb defects; sensorineural hearing loss 2/2. Cap excludes neurologic abnormalities, airway malformations and palatal cleft reported in 1/2.
Suppurative infection of the fallopian tube warrants the infection mechanism axis; the reproductive site has no organ axis.
Hereditary pulmonary cysts with neonatal pneumothorax; recurrent infections alone do not establish a separate immunodeficiency mechanism.
Retroperitoneal space has no dedicated axis; this heterogeneous cancer umbrella does not establish a particular visceral organ, vascular or locomotor tissue origin.
External ear and mandibular condyle malformations define the syndrome; corpus callosum hypoplasia and central apnea reported in 1/1 assessed patient support neurologic involvement.
Autoinflammatory osteitis, hyperostosis and synovitis with defining pustular/acneiform skin disease; intestinal inflammation, thrombosis and vasculitis occur in 5-29%.
Schizophrenia is a psychotic disorder excluded from the organ axes; genetic inheritance does not independently establish neurologic organ damage.
Idiopathic diffuse alveolar injury causes respiratory failure; infection or autoimmune disease is not established. Hypertension is not direct cardiovascular injury from AIP.
Malignant tumour originating in the glottic larynx; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary airway axis.
Bardet-Biedl subtype supports defining retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly; renal abnormalities/dysfunction occur in roughly 30-50%. Common neurodevelopmental involvement omitted by cap.
Familial azotemia reflects abnormal renal urea handling; isolated elevated urea does not establish progressive renal failure or damage to other organs.
Mixed malignant tumour of the uterine corpus; reproductive organ origin has no axis, and mesenchymal histology does not establish locomotor involvement.
Defining external ear, oral cleft and vision-impairing ocular abnormalities; kyphosis, pectus excavatum and cervical ribs occur in 30-79%, supporting skeletal involvement.
